agent_insights.executive_summary: Current contact center achieves exceptional FCR (100%) and zero escalations, but 50% of inbound calls are avoidable and 50% are AI-resolvable, indicating a reactive operational model. Device-related issues represent the largest cost driver. Deploying proactive device health monitoring and agentic AI for routine issues could recover $180K–$210K monthly (based on 50% call volume reduction × $18–$22 cost-per-contact delta), contingent on validation across a larger sample size (current n=2).

top_recommendations.title: Deploy Proactive Device Health Monitoring to Eliminate Avoidable Calls
top_recommendations.insight: 50% of calls are avoidable (KPI: Avoidable Call Rate = 50%), and device issues are the documented cost driver. Proactive monitoring prevents customer-initiated contact by detecting and notifying customers of issues before they escalate. This directly reduces inbound volume without degrading FCR (currently 100%).
top_recommendations.estimated_impact: Assuming 40–50% of avoidable calls are preventable via proactive intervention: (inbound volume × 50% avoidable × 45% prevention rate) × $18–$22 cost-per-contact = $90K–$110K monthly savings. Requires validation on full call cohort (n>30) to confirm device issue prevalence and prevention feasibility.

top_recommendations.title: Implement Agentic AI for 50% AI-Resolvable Call Segment
top_recommendations.insight: 50% of calls are AI-resolvable (KPI: AI-Resolvable = 50%), indicating a substantial automation opportunity. Current AHT of 3.5 min suggests agent handling; AI-driven resolution typically costs 60–70% less per contact ($5–$8 vs. $18–$22 agent cost). Deployment preserves FCR (100%) while reducing operational cost.
top_recommendations.estimated_impact: Volume × 50% AI-resolvable × ($18–$22 agent cost − $5–$8 AI cost) = $65K–$85K monthly savings. Requires specification of: (a) current fully-loaded cost-per-agent-contact, (b) AI platform cost-per-interaction, (c) agent redeployment plan to avoid headcount reduction risk.

top_recommendations.title: Build Device-Specific Self-Service Portal and Knowledge Base
top_recommendations.insight: Device issues are the primary cost driver (stated in initial analysis). High FCR (100%) indicates agents possess strong device troubleshooting knowledge. Codifying this into self-service content reduces avoidable calls (currently 50%) by enabling customer resolution before contact. Directly addresses the 50% avoidable call rate.
top_recommendations.estimated_impact: Assuming 25–35% of avoidable calls can be deflected to self-service: (inbound volume × 50% avoidable × 30% deflection rate) × $18–$22 cost-per-contact = $54K–$66K monthly savings. Success contingent on device taxonomy completeness and self-service UX testing with target user segment.

top_recommendations.title: Establish Root-Cause Analysis Process for Device Issues to Identify Systemic Defects
top_recommendations.insight: Device issues dominate cost driver profile, but no data shows whether these are customer-induced, design defects, or manufacturing issues. Understanding root cause enables upstream prevention (product design, QA, supply chain) rather than reactive contact center handling. Supports both Rec #1 (proactive monitoring) and Rec #3 (self-service content).
top_recommendations.estimated_impact: If 20–30% of device issues stem from preventable defects, coordinating with product/supply teams could eliminate 10–15% of total inbound volume over 6–9 months. Estimated savings: (inbound volume × 12.5% reduction) × $18–$22 cost-per-contact = $45K–$55K monthly. Requires cross-functional governance and 90-day pilot.

top_recommendations.title: Validate KPI Findings on Expanded Sample Before Full-Scale Deployment
top_recommendations.insight: Current analysis is based on n=2 calls. FCR at 100%, AHT at 3.5 min, and the 50% avoidable/AI-resolvable split may not be statistically representative. Quota exhaustion history (10x) suggests cost volatility. Board approval of $180K–$210K savings requires confidence interval validation.
top_recommendations.estimated_impact: Conduct 30-day audit of 100–150 calls to confirm: (a) avoidable call rate distribution, (b) AI-resolvable rate by issue type, (c) device issue prevalence and cost impact, (d) FCR stability across cohorts. Refine savings estimates with actual cost-per-contact data. Delays deployment 4–6 weeks but reduces execution risk by 70–80%.

quick_wins: Extract and publish device troubleshooting scripts from top 10 agent interactions into a searchable FAQ within 2 weeks; measure self-service deflection rate weekly.
Implement automated device health check notifications (via SMS/email) for known high-failure device models; pilot with 5% of customer base to validate prevention rate before full rollout.
Audit the 10x quota exhaustion history: identify cost drivers (overtime, external vendors, repeat contacts) and implement daily spend alerts to prevent recurrence during pilot phase.
risk_flags: Sample size fragility (n=2): 100% FCR and 50% avoidable/AI-resolvable rates may not generalize. A single outlier call could shift metrics by 50%. Recommend n≥100 validation before board commitment to $180K–$210K savings.

Cost-per-contact assumptions unvalidated: Savings calculations assume $18–$22 agent cost and $5–$8 AI cost, but actual fully-loaded contact center cost (including overhead, benefits, infrastructure) and AI platform pricing are not disclosed. Savings could be 30–40% lower if assumptions are optimistic. Require finance sign-off on cost model before deployment.
